doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Freelancing, Europe and touring with Preservation Hall
summary: After Hampton he subbed around, toured Europe, and from about 1987 toured more with Preservation Hall as Percy Humphrey aged.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. But it was all part of it. And that was a great experience. Wallace Davenport was right, he was right. He said, “Man, no matter what kind of money they offer you just take it.” So yeah, it was a great, great opportunity and preparation. So I kind of started like substituting for different people. I did a lot of European trips. Chet Baker and I had the same manager, Vim Vict from Vhagony & Holland. So he had booked me some nice gigs over there, you know some traditional gigs, some kind of swing gigs and bop gigs and stuff like that. Then I kind of started traveling with the Preservation Hall band like really about 1987. I had done a few trips with them before that but it’s when the old guy Percy Humphrey really started getting old, I started doing more and more touring with them. But I still enjoy getting out on my own. I mean that’s the kind of house buying job which we all need, thank God they’re there sometimes. But sometimes you want a little more freedom of expression and sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t.
